_comment: Adopter-owned configuration for /cadence-sync-jira (BTG-075 AC-7). Every value that varies per repository or per Jira instance lives here; nothing instance-varying is hardcoded in a script or in skill prose. jira-lib.sh is the single resolver, so each key's fail-loud/default polarity is defined exactly once (see jira-server-scripts.md section 4).

status_workflow_map._comment_cancelled_row: RETARGET NOTE for the `cancelled` rows in this map and in `assignment_map` (BTG-262). `cancelled` is the repo lifecycle's terminal-without-merge status: the ticket ended and no code came of it. It ships mapped to `Done` as a DOCUMENTED DEFAULT, NOT A VERIFIED ONE -- `Done` is a status these blocks already declare, which is why it was chosen over inventing a `Won't Fix`-shaped value that may not exist in the scheme at all. NO `global_transitions` id is declared for it: an id cannot be verified from the framework repository, and a wrong id fires a real transition with real post-functions and notifications, so omitting one is strictly safer than guessing one. The observed multi-hop walk in jira-transition.sh is therefore the only path to it, and adding these rows is what widens DECLARED_STATUSES so that walk may step through `Done` at all. WIDENING HAZARD -- STATED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED (DEC-023). These rows are NOT inert for the eight statuses this change does not touch. `js_config_workflow_statuses` in jira-lib.sh derives DECLARED_STATUSES from ALL VALUES of an issue type's block, and jira-transition.sh bounds its multi-hop walk by that set. `Done` was already declared for Task and Issue, but NOT for Bug or Story, whose declared set was {To Do, Planning, Awaiting Implementation, In Progress, Code Review, Pending Deployment} and now also carries `Done`. Two consequences follow, both on statuses these rows never mention: (i) a governed onward hop that used to be UNIQUE may now be AMBIGUOUS, in which case jira-transition.sh HALTS syncjs.transition.unreachable and a merged Bug that used to project refuses -- loud rather than silent, which is why this is recorded rather than worked around; and (ii) where there was previously no governed hop, `Done` may now BE the unique one, so a merely MERGED Bug or Story is stepped THROUGH `Done`, firing whatever post-function your instance attaches to it -- this repository's own live run observed exactly that on its reference instance, which set a resolution by post-function rather than by request. NEITHER CONSEQUENCE WAS VERIFIED AGAINST ANY ADOPTER WORKFLOW SCHEME and neither is claimed safe there; the live run that did happen exercised a single one-hop To Do -> Done and never entered the walk branch at all. IF YOUR SCHEME ROUTES BUG OR STORY ANYWHERE NEAR `Done`, READ THOSE TWO BLOCKS BEFORE YOUR FIRST SYNC. AN ADOPTER WHOSE SCHEME CANNOT REACH `Done` FROM A BUG OR A STORY RETARGETS THESE ROWS in their own copy -- that is what this file is for. Nothing here is a claim about your instance; it is this repository's own choice, stated so you can change it. (This note is sited INSIDE the map it annotates, deliberately: btg-102-retype-guard.test.sh S-1.2 builds a workflow-free fixture by deleting this map and then requires that no mention of a workflow survives, which is what makes its pin non-vacuous. A note about this map belongs in this map.)
